newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids hold but bears eye mild weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids hold but bears eye mild weather.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices, helped by prospects for better utility demand after the recent heat, held fairly steady Monday, but activity was quiet and forecasts for mild weather through the month roused the bears.

"Utilities have been burning a lot of oil, but temps are supposed to stay more normal. I don't think we'll see any more upside unless we get another heat wave," said one cash trader, adding prices could fall once utilities replenish stocks.
East Coast temperatures are not expected to vary much from normal right through the month, according the National Weather Service.

In New York Harbor, physical one percent was unchanged at about $17.25 a barrel, with August one percent paper down almost 50 cents to the $16.50 area. Traders said September paper was quoted at $16.10-20, while Q4 was pegged at $16.60-70.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour also was little changed at $18.25-50, with expected late-month supplies and competitive city gate gas prices likely to cap any upside near-term.
High sulphurs in New York were steady, with 2.2 percent still talked near $15.50.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices remained stable, with one percent still in the low-$16s and three percent at $14.50-75.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.

New York city gate swing gas prices stumbled 15 cents Monday to $2.40/mmBtu, or $15.12 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, skidded almost a dime to $2.17/mmBtu, or $13.67 a barrel.
